annotation.title_clean: Rwanda Civil Aviation Regulations Part 27: Unmanned Aircraft Systems
annotation.title_en: Rwanda Civil Aviation Regulations Part 27: Unmanned Aircraft Systems
annotation.summary_en: Rwanda's binding Part 27 of the Civil Aviation Regulations, issued as Special Regulations RSR/01/2026, governs unmanned aircraft systems. It sets risk-based basic and specific categories, registration, remote pilot and operator certification, BVLOS and highly automated operations, manufacturer declarations, UTM, security vetting, insurance, and privacy rules.
key_provisions_or_claims: Two-tier classification: Basic operations (notification, 1 kg limit) and Specific operations (authorization, operator certificate, pilot licence, 25 kg limit).
BVLOS requires authorization based on air and ground risk assessment, detect-and-avoid, and area approval with 90-day application (Subpart I).
Highly automated UAS operations require consultation with the National Civil Aviation Security Committee, which sets security conditions.
Mandatory UAS registration, security vetting of pilots and owners, and third-party liability insurance; military-specification UAS barred.
Privacy rules ban non-consensual surveillance and restrict thermal imaging; operators must run safety management systems and report accidents within 24 hours.
